a.stop: Back to the radar's own app
adc.lead: Settings for the raw data stream used by your own algorithms. Live raw data goes to a PC over USB; here you set the radar up and test the data link.
b2b: Volume, pre-flashed modules or custom firmware: Kymopsis B2B
bt.bak.d: Slower (about 8 s more per module); off for new blank modules.
bt.lead: Choose a firmware once. Each module is flashed as soon as it is connected; swap modules when the light turns blue.
c.period.d: Frame period 0 = as fast as possible.
dg.lead: Quick checks when something does not work. The log below shows what Radar Base and the radar report.
f.fall.d: A fall was detected. Check on the person.
f.h.d: Ceiling mount, facing down. Measure from the floor to the radar.
f.none.d: Nobody is in the detection area.
f.normal.d: Someone is in the room; no fall detected.
fall.lead: Watches for falls and tells whether someone is in the room.
fi.d: Radar apps and backups stored on Radar Base.
fl.confirm: Write {app} into the radar's flash? The current firmware is backed up first.
fl.lead: Puts an app into the radar's own flash so it starts by itself at power-up. The current firmware is saved first and can be put back at any time.
fl.open.d: This is the open firmware. It runs every radar app from the radar's memory (see Run a scenario) but does not write the radar's flash. Writing needs the dev-kit firmware.
fl.rest.d: Puts a saved firmware back exactly as it was.
fl.s1.d: Apps are files stored on Radar Base. Add new ones under Device settings → Firmware files.
fl.s2.d: The radar's current firmware is backed up first (saved as bakN.bin). If the backup fails, nothing is written. Takes about 15 seconds.
foot.med: Wellness use only, not a medical device.
hd3d.lead: Live positions from the radar. Each dot is a person; areas light up when someone is inside.
help.ceiling: Radar on the ceiling facing down, 2.2–3 m above the floor. The view is a floor plan with the radar in the middle.
help.side: Radar on a wall about 1.5 m high, facing into the room. The view is the ±55° area in front of it.
home.lead: Radar Base is connected. The radar is running: {app}.
home.title: What would you like to do?
hs.b2b: Volume and custom firmware: Kymopsis B2B
hs.guides: Guides: setup, Home Assistant, ESPHome, JSON
hs.inst.d: Put the open firmware on an ESP32-S3 board, straight from the browser.
hs.lead: Connect a Kymopsis Radar Base to use it right here. Nothing is sent to the cloud.
hs.net.d: Board already on your Wi-Fi? Open its own page at kymradar.local.
hs.nocloud: No cloud: everything runs on your board and your network.
hs.note: USB needs Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer. On phones and other browsers, use the board over Wi-Fi.
hs.product: Get a Radar Base dev kit
hs.title: Radar Base in your browser
hs.usb.d: Plug the board into this computer and pick its port. Chrome or Edge on a desktop.
kit.only: Included with the Kymopsis development kit firmware.
mq.d: Send results to your own MQTT broker, for example the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant. Radar Base appears in Home Assistant by itself.
mq.keep: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
mq.st.on: Connected to {host}. Home Assistant discovery sent.
mq.st.wifi: Waits for the home Wi-Fi, then connects to {host}.
ovl.load.d: Sending the app to the radar, about 6 seconds.
ovl.wait.d: If nothing appears, check that the radar is powered.
run.lead: It loads into the radar's memory in about 6 seconds. Power-cycling the radar returns it to the app in its flash.
run.title: Choose a scenario
sc.fall.d: Flags a fall and whether someone is present. Ceiling mount.
sc.flash: The app already in the radar
sc.flash.d: Restart the radar from its flash and show what it reports.
sc.hd3d.d: Where people are in the room, up to several at once, with 4 occupancy areas. Ceiling or wall mount.
sc.vital.d: One person sitting or lying still, 0.5–1.5 m in front of the radar.
set.lead: Connect Radar Base to your home Wi-Fi, manage firmware files and check the device.
st.d: Runs the raw-data app for a few seconds and checks every block arriving from the radar.
t.busy: The radar is busy, try again in a few seconds
t.rej: Not accepted, see the note below
task.adc.d: Chirp, gain and filter settings, plus a data-link self-test. Live raw data needs USB.
task.batch.d: Write the same firmware to many modules in a row: detect, write, verify, PASS / FAIL, CSV log.
task.flash.d: Make an app start by itself at power-up. The current firmware is backed up first.
task.run.d: Load a ready-made radar app and watch live results. The radar's flash is not changed.
task.set.d: Wi-Fi, firmware files, language and diagnostics.
tr.d: Writing the radar's flash is done by a small closed module that is part of the dev-kit firmware only. That is its only job: it does not connect to the internet and collects no data. Everything else is open source, and every radar app can also run from memory without it.
usb.nofiles: Managing files needs Wi-Fi: open the app from Radar Base itself.
usb.space: Over USB, network names and passwords cannot contain spaces. Use Wi-Fi for those.
v.range: Floor area shown (± from the radar)
v.tips.d: Sit or lie still, 0.5–1.5 m in front of the radar, chest facing it. The first values appear after about 20 seconds.
vital.lead: Breathing and heart rate of one person sitting or lying still.
wf.forget.q: Forget the saved home network? The hotspot will turn on.
wf.help: Once connected, open http://kymradar.local (or the address shown above) from any device on the same Wi-Fi. The Radar Base hotspot only turns on when no home network is saved or it cannot be reached.
wf.joining: Joining… this page may move to the new address
wf.name: Network name
